title.en: Present findings to a study group
title.es: Presentar hallazgos a un grupo de estudio

es: Presentar ante un grupo de estudio los hallazgos de un estudio: resumirlos con fidelidad, dar una conclusión cautelosa y responder a una objeción reconociendo sus límites.

teaching.en: Let me summarise the study: two hundred students kept a sleep diary for a month.
teaching.es: Permítanme resumir el estudio: doscientos estudiantes llevaron un diario de sueño durante un mes.
teaching.explanationEs: Let me summarise + datos principales: el resumen es fiel, sin opinión.
segments: Let me summarise the study: two hundred students
kept a sleep diary for a month.
teaching.audioText: Let me summarise the study: two hundred students kept a sleep diary for a month.

teaching.en: The main findings suggest that students who sleep more tend to score higher.
teaching.es: Los principales hallazgos sugieren que los estudiantes que duermen más suelen sacar mejores notas.
teaching.explanationEs: Findings + suggest: la conclusión cautelosa basada en los resultados.
segments: The main findings suggest that students who
sleep more tend to score higher.
teaching.audioText: The main findings suggest that students who sleep more tend to score higher.

teaching.en: One limitation is that the sample was small, so the findings may not apply to everyone.
teaching.es: Una limitación es que la muestra era pequeña, así que los hallazgos podrían no aplicarse a todo el mundo.
teaching.explanationEs: Limitation: un punto débil del estudio; admitirlo da credibilidad.
segments: One limitation is that the sample was small,
so the findings may not apply to everyone.
teaching.audioText: One limitation is that the sample was small, so the findings may not apply to everyone.

teaching.en: That is a fair point, but the results are still likely to be valid for this age group.
teaching.es: Es un punto razonable, pero los resultados probablemente siguen siendo válidos para este grupo de edad.
teaching.explanationEs: Fair point reconoce la objeción; valid defiende la conclusión con cautela.
segments: That is a fair point, but the results are
still likely to be valid for this age group.
teaching.audioText: That is a fair point, but the results are still likely to be valid for this age group.

teaching.en: Nevertheless, more research is needed before we can be sure.
teaching.es: Aun así, hace falta más investigación antes de poder estar seguros.
teaching.explanationEs: Nevertheless introduce el contraste; no se combina con but.
teaching.audioText: Nevertheless, more research is needed before we can be sure.

teaching.en: Her reply to the objection was calm: the diary method is widely used.
teaching.es: Su respuesta a la objeción fue tranquila: el método del diario se usa mucho.
teaching.explanationEs: Reply to + objection: responder con un argumento, no a la defensiva.
segments: Her reply to the objection was calm:
the diary method is widely used.
teaching.audioText: Her reply to the objection was calm: the diary method is widely used.

prompt.es: Elige la frase que resume un estudio con fidelidad.

choices.text: Let me summarise: all students prefer the library.
Let me summarise: in a survey of 120 students, 54 percent preferred studying in the library.
Let me summarise: the library is the best place, in my opinion.

feedback.es: Un resumen fiel repite lo que dice el estudio (120 estudiantes, 54 por ciento) sin exagerar ni añadir opiniones; las otras frases generalizan o dan una opinión.

hint.es: Busca la frase que mantiene la cifra y no generaliza.

origin.text: A survey of 120 students found that 54 percent prefer studying in the library.

feedback.es: A fair point reconoce que la objeción es razonable; fair es el adjetivo que significa justo o razonable.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Una limitación es que la muestra era pequeña.»

answer.text: One limitation is that the sample was small

feedback.es: One limitation is that + idea presenta un punto débil del estudio: que la muestra era pequeña.

prompt.es: Un compañero objeta: «The sample is too small.» Elige la mejor respuesta.

choices.text: You are wrong, and the sample is perfect.
I prefer not to talk about the sample.
That is a fair point; nevertheless, the findings suggest a pattern.

feedback.es: That is a fair point; nevertheless… reconoce la objeción y mantiene una conclusión cautelosa. Las otras dos respuestas atacan a quien pregunta o evitan el tema.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige la limitación que admite la presentadora.

choices.text: Only students took part in the study.

feedback.es: La presentadora dice que todos los participantes eran estudiantes: esa es la limitación que admite antes de mantener su conclusión con cautela.

origin.audio: Thanks for the question. One limitation of the study is that all the participants were students. Nevertheless, the findings suggest that short breaks may improve attention.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada fórmula con su función en la presentación.

feedback.es: Let me summarise abre el resumen, One limitation is that admite un punto débil, That is a fair point reconoce la objeción y Nevertheless mantiene la conclusión.

prompt.es: Una compañera dice: «Your study only asked 30 people.» Elige tu respuesta.

choices.text: No, thirty people is enough and nobody can question it.
Yes, that is a limitation; nevertheless, the results may still be valid.
I agree, so the findings are not valid at all.

feedback.es: Reconocer que es una limitación y añadir nevertheless con may es la respuesta cauta; las otras dos niegan el problema o tiran abajo todo el estudio.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué objeción menciona la oradora.

choices.text: The study lasted too many months.
Cyclists might have been healthier before the study.

feedback.es: La oradora dice que los ciclistas podrían ser ya más sanos antes del estudio: esa es la objeción que reconoce, no una conclusión suya.

origin.audio: To summarise, the authors followed one hundred cyclists for six months. Their findings suggest that cycling to work may reduce stress. One objection is that cyclists may already be healthier.

prompt.es: Completa con «limitación» y «sin embargo» (en inglés) las dos frases.

feedback.es: Limitation nombra un punto débil del estudio y nevertheless (o however) introduce la conclusión que se mantiene tras reconocer la objeción.

sentences: One ___ of the study is that the sample was small.
That is a fair point; ___, the results are likely to be valid.

prompt.es: Escribe tu presentación: resume, concluye con cautela y responde.

answer.text: Good morning, everyone. Let me summarise our study. One hundred and fifty students kept a study diary for a month. The students who reviewed their notes every day scored twelve percent higher in a final test than the others. The findings suggest that daily review may help students remember more, and this seems to be true for most subjects. Some of you may have an objection, so let me reply to one of them: a classmate said that these students were probably more interested already. That is a fair point, and it is a limitation of the study. To a certain extent, you may be right. Nevertheless, the difference was large, and it is likely to be valid for students of our age. More research is needed before we can be sure, but I would suggest trying daily review this month. Thank you for listening.
accepted: Good morning, everyone. Let me summarise our study. One hundred and fifty students kept a study diary for a month. The students who reviewed their notes every day scored twelve percent higher in a final test than the others. The findings suggest that daily review may help students remember more, and this seems to be true for most subjects. Some of you may have an objection, so let me reply to one of them: a classmate said that these students were probably more interested already. That is a fair point, and it is a limitation of the study. To a certain extent, you may be right. Nevertheless, the difference was large, and it is likely to be valid for students of our age. More research is needed before we can be sure, but I would suggest trying daily review this month. Thank you for listening.

Hello, everyone. To summarise, 150 students wrote in a study diary every day for a month. After the month, the students who reviewed their notes daily scored twelve percent higher in the final test. The results suggest that regular review might improve memory. Someone has asked whether these students were already more interested. That is a good point, and I accept it as a limitation. It could be argued that interested students simply study more. However, the findings still seem to show a clear effect, so I think the conclusion is likely to be valid, although we need more research. For now, I would suggest that we all try daily review for one month, and then compare our scores. Thank you for your attention.

feedback.es: Una buena respuesta resume el estudio con fidelidad, da una conclusión con recursos de cautela, reconoce la objeción como razonable y mantiene la conclusión.

origin.text: Resume un estudio para tu grupo, da una conclusión cautelosa y responde a una objeción. Estudio: 150 estudiantes llevaron un diario de estudio durante un mes; los que repasaron cada día sacaron un 12 % más en una prueba final. Objeción de una compañera: «Puede que esos estudiantes ya fueran más motivados.» Escribe entre 120 y 180 palabras: un resumen fiel, una conclusión con al menos dos recursos de cautela y una respuesta a la objeción.

prompt.es: Elige la respuesta que mantiene la conclusión tras una objeción.

choices.text: That is a fair point. Nevertheless, the findings still suggest a link.
That is a fair point, so the findings are useless.
Nevertheless, but the findings prove everything.

feedback.es: That is a fair point… nevertheless… suggest reconoce el punto y sigue defendiendo el hallazgo con cautela; las otras respuestas anulan el estudio o repiten un error de conectores.

answer.text: Let me summarise the main findings

feedback.es: Let me summarise the main findings abre un resumen: summarise es el verbo y main findings los resultados más importantes.

prompt.es: Completa: «Los autores concluyen que el ejercicio puede mejorar el ánimo.»

feedback.es: Conclude that + idea con may es la fórmula de la conclusión cautelosa en un resumen; con The authors el verbo no lleva -s.

origin.text: The authors ___ that exercise may improve mood.
